# Structural pass against the Google Rust style guide

Status: Proposed

Google's Rust style guide (https://google.github.io/styleguide/rustguide.html) was read in full and compared with the workspace. Formatting that rustfmt and clippy already cover is out of scope. The gaps that cost maintenance are: non-leaf modules that still hold the implementation, a handful of files past the repo's own ~800 non-test-line rule, and error types that store another error but do not expose it through Error::source. Chromium-only rules (flat crate layout, no async, no std threads, tiny crates) do not fit this Cargo project and are not adopted. This plan is the record of that judgment. It does not change launcher behavior.

## Scope

- In: A shrinking allowlist so non-test Rust files under crates/ stop growing past about 800 lines.
- In: Error::source on variants that already store another error, without changing Display text.
- In: Splits of non-leaf modules that still implement the API: model_view, world_explorer, schematic_studio.
- In: Splits where one file already has two concerns: settings (accounts and launcher settings), the replace dialog, the instance intent router, and plugin-tab rendering.
- Out: Behavior changes, copy changes, and IA path changes. Moved // ia comments stay byte-for-byte; just ia must not rewrite docs/ia/paths.
- Out: A thiserror or anyhow migration, and retyping ServiceError::Install(String) or ServiceError::Remote(String).
- Out: UI-thread unwrap and expect cleanup. That stays on error-reporting T5.
- Out: Splitting InstanceStore (crates/lumilio-core/src/instance.rs) or the release manifest (crates/lumilio-core/src/release.rs) only to hit a line count.
- Out: New crates, a flat Chromium layout, workspace missing_docs, unwrap_used, or blanket #[non_exhaustive].
- Out: forks/, vendor/, and tools/entity-dump (the Java dumper is one class beside its Rust reader and is not a Rust-style target).

## Decision D1

Keep the Cargo layout and the current crate split. Do not flatten sources into one directory per crate, and do not break lumilio-core or lumilio-ui into smaller crates for style.

Why: The guide marks flat layout and tiny crates as Chromium rules. They exist for a GN build graph, not for Cargo. This repo already has many small crates (transfer, nbt, anvil, plugin-api, one crate per plugin). lumilio-core is about 77k lines and lumilio-ui about 86k because AGENTS.md puts domain logic in core and pages in ui. lib.rs is 253 lines and 64 pub use lines: the root already re-exports the public surface and keeps child modules private, which is the part of the guide worth keeping.

Consequences: Compile times and dependency direction stay as they are. A new crate still needs a dependency-direction reason, not a style reason.

## Decision D2

Keep async, tokio, std::thread workers, Arc, and Rc. Keep catch_unwind around plugin calls and the schematic preview worker.

Why: The guide's bans on async and std threads are Chromium rules. The launcher is a tokio app; GPUI callbacks are not Send, so Rc is the honest tool; shared download and plugin state is Arc. catch_unwind in crates/lumilio-core/src/plugins/mod.rs and crates/lumilio-ui/src/model_view/worker.rs is the guide's own defense-in-depth exception: a plugin or a mesher panic must not kill the process. Google forbids relying on it for correctness. This code does not: the panic becomes Fault or a failed preview.

Consequences: No task replaces these. A new catch_unwind still needs the same isolation reason.

## Decision D3

Do not enable missing_docs, unwrap_used, non_exhaustive, or rustfmt imports_granularity for the workspace. Do not rename domain abbreviations.

Why: publish is false and one team owns every crate. missing_docs would demand comments the guide itself says to omit when the name is enough. unwrap in production is mostly inside #[cfg(test)] modules that share a file with the code; the UI-thread cases are already error-reporting T5. non_exhaustive matters across teams. Plugins are in-tree; API_VERSION is 1. If wasm-plugin-registry ships external plugins, that plan owns stability attributes. imports_granularity is formatting. Nbt, Motd, and similar names are the domain's names.

Consequences: plugin-api stays an ordinary Rust API until an external plugin boundary exists. Clippy stays at the workspace denies (dbg_macro, todo, unimplemented) plus rustfmt.

## Decision D4

Do not adopt thiserror. Do not retype stringly service errors. Do implement source() for stored errors.

Why: Display strings are the sentences people read. A derive migration would move that copy for no behavior change, and error-reporting already left a thiserror migration out. ServiceError::Install(String) and Remote(String) are the boundary where TransferError, ModpackError, and most DiscoverError values become one sentence; callers match Cancelled and the typed variants and print to_string(). TransportError is already a string because http.rs runs with_causes before wrapping, which is how DNS and TLS text is kept. Empty impl Error for … {} still drops the chain wherever a typed error is stored: ServiceError::source is empty, so a walk stops at the service even when StoreError holds an io::Error.

Consequences: T2 is additive and display-neutral. A later caller that must branch on install failures changes the enum in that feature's plan, not in this one.

## Decision D5

Leave three files on the allowlist after the splits: instance.rs, release.rs, and backdrop.rs.

Why: instance.rs is one InstanceStore (schema version 6). release.rs is one manifest model plus inheritance, and it is already named after that item. backdrop.rs is the rejected visual experiment compiled only under cfg(test). Cutting them up would not separate a second concern. The other eight files are either non-leaf modules full of implementation (the guide's rule, and the 800-line rule) or already mix two concerns.

Consequences: T1's list shrinks to those three paths and no further. A new oversized file fails the test instead of joining the list.

## Decision D6

Leave unsafe where it is.

Why: The workspace forbids unsafe_code. lumilio-cubiomes, lumilio-pointer, and lumilio-backdrop opt into deny and keep the unsafe in ffi.rs, macos.rs, and windows.rs, with SAFETY comments. That is the guide's isolation rule. The Java entity dumper is not Rust.

Consequences: No task moves FFI. New unsafe still has to live in one of those crates or justify a new one.
